pairs.subject: agent-memory
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/templates.rs:207 The autonomous directive still sets a per-run quota of 1-3 durable memories. dispatch.rs writes each one straight into persona_memories via mem_repo::create, so every run mints consolidated beliefs inline. Nothing goes through a batched, judged distillation pass, and this contradicts the assembler's own 'If it won't change a future decision, don't store it' (assemble.rs:660).

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/templates.rs:207 Consolidation should be a batch over episodes with hindsight. Here a quota forces inline writes to the durable layer, and the preamble line 33 ('Treat memory writes as compounding') pushes the agent to hoard.

src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/templates.rs:23 Claims about the human (preference) go through the same auto-commit door as world facts. dispatch.rs:997 calls mem_repo::create with no proposal/pending lane, so a belief about the user is recalled as settled without review.

src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/assemble.rs:28 The recency bridge (Recent Episodes) has its own small cap, separate from other sections. Only that tier is visible in this context; relevance-tier recall lives elsewhere.
src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/assemble.rs:625 Episodes are injected as fenced records ('memory/data only'), high as record and low as belief, not as instructions.

pairs.evidence: src/features/companions/athena/decision/rosterDecisions.ts:101 The orb's approval prompt renders only the action label and rationale. The write_fact params (scope incl. user, value, sources per catalog.rs:638) ride in an unrendered payload, and write_fact is classified LOW_RISK (actionRisk.ts:50), so the orb recommends approve. A durable belief, possibly about the user, gets adopted without the reviewer seeing the value or its grounds.

techniques.evidence: src/features/companions/athena/decision/rosterDecisions.ts:101 The proposal-reviewed lane requires the item to be visible and editable to the operator. Here the review surface hides the belief content and sources.
